# Daḷhadhammajātaka (Ja 409)

**ID:** Ja 409  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Daḷhadhammajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul6.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul6.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Daḷhadhammajātaka* (Ja 409) is a canonical birth story found in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. According to the narrative framework, the Buddha related this story while dwelling in the Ghosita forest (Ghosikārāma) near Kosambī, occasioned by the mistreatment and neglect of Bhaddavatikā, the royal she-elephant of King Udena [Fausböll 1883].

In the story of the past, a monarch named Daḷhadhamma ruled in Benares, served by the Bodhisatta as his most trusted minister [Cowell 1897]. The king possessed a mighty she-elephant who had performed extraordinary services in her prime, travelling a hundred leagues in a day and executing royal errands, but upon growing old she was abandoned and deprived of her honours [Cowell 1897; UNDV Conference 2009]. Observing her neglected state, the Bodhisatta admonished the king with verses emphasizing the moral duty of gratefulness and reciprocal care [Anandajoti 2010; UNDV Conference 2009]. He warned that anyone who fails to acknowledge past benefactions will find no aid when misfortune strikes in the future [Anandajoti 2010]. Moved by the Bodhisatta’s counsel, the king restored the elephant's past privileges, practiced generosity and good deeds, and attained rebirth in heaven [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. In the birth identification (*samodhāna*), the she-elephant is identified as Bhaddavatikā, King Daḷhadhamma as Ānanda, and the wise minister as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883].

**Sources**

- [Fausböll 1883] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with its commentary, Vol. 3 (1883) — Pali opening setting, canonical framing, verse introduction, and the concluding samodhāna identification.
- [Cowell 1897] E. B. Cowell (ed.), The Jātaka, or Stories of the Buddha’s Former Births, Vol. 3 (1897) — Narrative summary of King Daḷhadhamma, the Bodhisatta as minister, and the neglected she-elephant.
- [Anandajoti 2010] Bhikkhu Ānandajoti, Buddhist Wisdom Verses: 551 Verses from the Canon (2010) — Verse translation on gratefulness and synopsis of the Bodhisatta's admonition.
- [UNDV Conference 2009] UNDV Conference Volume, Buddhist Approach to Environmental Crisis (2009) — Discussion of the Jātaka's ethical theme of care and gratitude toward aging animals.
